key_insight: CuAD generates tangent and adjoint CUDA kernels directly from source, enabling accurate GPU-based flow sensitivities with adjoint runtimes of 2–6 times the primal kernels.
engineering_relevance: The tool supports aerodynamic shape optimization and data assimilation by differentiating GPU flow solvers, including residuals, boundary conditions and wall forces.
method: Transforms CUDA kernels into ordinary CUDA tangent and adjoint source.
Organizes reverse mode around individual GPU threads, assuming non-aliasing inputs and outputs.
Recomputes intermediates, differentiates pure accumulations without a tape and stores remaining tape in fixed thread-local arrays.
evidence_signal: Across four flow-model kernels and a 2D Euler solver, derivatives passed dot-product tests to round-off; transonic NACA 0012 adjoint sensitivities agreed with tangents to 10⁻¹³.
watch_item: Deployment requires preserving the input/output non-aliasing assumption and checking fixed thread-local tape requirements for new kernels.
paper_title: CuAD: Source-to-Source Automatic Differentiation of CUDA Kernels for Discrete Adjoints in Computational Fluid Dynamics
